issues.legal_issue: A court must direct the submission of a statement of case when an arguable question of law arises from the tribunal’s order, even if the question’s eventual answer is uncertain.
material_facts: The tax tribunal interpreted the trust deed’s directions concerning a share of income and held that the income was exempt from tax.
The tribunal declined to refer the question concerning that share of income, and the High Court rejected an application seeking an order requiring the reference.
The legal effect of the trust deed’s directions raised a question of law arising from the tribunal’s order.
The appeal challenged the High Court’s refusal to direct the reference.
issues.conclusion: The Supreme Court set aside the High Court’s order and directed it to call upon the tribunal to submit a statement of case on the question concerning the tax exemption of the disputed share of income. It did not decide whether that income was ultimately exempt.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 66(2) of the Indian Income-tax Act, 1922, the High Court considering an application to require a reference must decide whether a question of law that may be supported by reasonable argument arises out of the tribunal’s order. It is not to decide at that stage whether the question will ultimately be answered in favour of the assessee. No earlier cases are relied on in the judgment.

predicates.appeal_from_refusal_to_order_reference: The proceeding is an appeal against a court’s refusal to require a tribunal to submit a statement of case.
predicates.tribunal_interpreted_trust_direction: The tribunal interpreted a direction in a trust instrument when deciding the tax treatment of income.
predicates.arguable_law_question_from_order: A question about the legal effect of the direction, capable of reasonable argument, arose from the tribunal’s order.
predicates.reference_must_be_ordered: The court must require the tribunal to submit a statement of case on the arguable question of law.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges a refusal to order a reference and the tribunal’s interpretation of a trust direction gives rise to an arguable question of law, the reference must be ordered.
